There are three common scales to measure temperature: Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F), and Kelvin (K). The Celsius scale is based on the freezing and boiling points of water, while the Fahrenheit scale has a wider range. The Kelvin scale is absolute and starts from absolute zero.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Law of Conservation of Mass
text:
Law of Conservation of Mass

Key terms: law of conservation of mass, reactants, products, mass

The law of conservation of mass states that in any chemical reaction, the total mass of the reactants is equal to the total mass of the products. This means that matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Law of Conservation of Mass in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Law of Definite Proportions
text:
Law of Definite Proportions

Key terms: law of definite proportions, compound, mass ratio

The law of definite proportions states that a given compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by mass. This means that the mass ratio of the elements in a compound is always the same.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Law of Definite Proportions in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Law of Conservation of Mass
text:
Law of Conservation of Mass

Key terms: matter, conservation, Lavoisier

Matter cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. This law was established by Lavoisier through precise measurements and experiments.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Law of Conservation of Mass in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Gay Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes
text:
Gay Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes

Key terms: gases, volumes, Gay Lussac, Avogadro

Gases combine or decompose in simple, whole-number ratios by volume, provided they are at the same temperature and pressure. This law was discovered by Gay Lussac and later explained by Avogadro.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Gay Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gay Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Avogadro's Law
text:
Avogadro's Law

Key terms: Avogadro, molecules, volumes

Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules. This law was proposed by Avogadro and helps explain Gay Lussac's law.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Avogadro's Law in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Law of Definite Proportions
text:
Law of Definite Proportions

Key terms: compound, elements, Proust

A given compound always contains the same proportion of elements by mass. This law was given by Proust and is also known as the Law of Definite Composition.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Law of Definite Proportions in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Law of Multiple Proportions
text:
Law of Multiple Proportions

Key terms: elements, compounds, Dalton

If two elements can combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in the ratio of small whole numbers. This law was proposed by Dalton.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Law of Multiple Proportions in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Atomic Mass
text:
Atomic Mass

Key terms: atom, mass, amu, u, carbon-12

The mass of an atom is extremely small and is measured in atomic mass units (amu) or unified mass units (u). Carbon-12 is used as the standard for atomic masses.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Atomic Mass in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Mole Concept
text:
Mole Concept

Key terms: mole, amount, entities

A mole is a unit used to measure the amount of a substance. One mole contains exactly 6.022 × 10^23 elementary entities (atoms, molecules, etc.).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Mole Concept in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Percentage Composition
text:

The percentage of each element in a compound can be calculated using the formula: (mass of the element in the compound / molar mass of the compound) × 100.

metadata.subject: Chemistry

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Molar Mass Calculation
text:

Molar mass is calculated by adding the atomic masses of all atoms in a compound. It's the mass of one mole of a substance.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Moles to Mass Conversion
text:

Key terms: moles, molar mass, mass

To convert moles to mass, multiply the number of moles by the molar mass of the substance. To convert mass to moles, divide the mass by the molar mass.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Moles to Mass Conversion in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Empirical Formula
text:
Empirical Formula

Key terms: empirical formula, mole ratio, compound

The empirical formula of a compound is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms present in the compound. It's found by dividing the moles of each element by the smallest mole ratio.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Empirical Formula in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Molecular Formula
text:
Molecular Formula

Key terms: molecular formula, empirical formula, molar mass

The molecular formula of a compound is the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule of the compound. It's found by multiplying the empirical formula by a factor 'n' to match the molar mass.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Molecular Formula in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Balanced Chemical Equation
text:
Balanced Chemical Equation

Key terms: balanced equation, coefficients, reactants, products

A balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides of the equation. It's balanced by adding coefficients to the reactants and products.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Balanced Chemical Equation in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Limiting Reagent
text:
Limiting Reagent

Key terms: limiting reagent, stoichiometry, balanced equation

The limiting reagent is the reactant that gets consumed first and limits the amount of product formed. It's identified by comparing the mole ratios of reactants with the stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced equation.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Limiting Reagent in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Molarity Calculation
text:
Molarity Calculation

Key terms: molarity, moles, volume, concentration

Molarity is calculated by dividing the number of moles of solute by the volume of the solution in liters. It's used to prepare solutions of a desired concentration.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Molarity Calculation in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Dilution of Solutions

Dilution is the process of reducing the concentration of a solution by adding solvent. The number of moles of solute remains constant, but the volume of the solution increases.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Dilution of Solutions in Grade 11 Chemistry.

The combination of different atoms is governed by basic laws such as the Law of Conservation of Mass, Law of Definite Proportions, Law of Multiple Proportions, Gay Lussac’s Law of Gaseous Volumes, and Avogadro Law.

The atomic mass of an element is expressed relative to the 12C isotope of carbon, and the molecular mass of a molecule is obtained by taking the sum of the atomic masses of different atoms present in a molecule.

Mole and Avogadro Constant

The number of atoms, molecules, or any other particles present in a given system are expressed in terms of the Avogadro constant (6.022 × 10^23). This is known as 1 mol of the respective particles or entities.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Mole and Avogadro Constant in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Chemical Reactions and Stoichiometry

Key terms: chemical reactions, balanced equation, stoichiometry, molar ratios

A balanced chemical equation provides information about the molar ratios and the respective number of particles taking part in a particular reaction. Stoichiometry is the quantitative study of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.

Concentration of Solutions

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Discovery of Electron
text:
Discovery of Electron

Electrons were discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897 using cathode ray tubes. They are negatively charged particles with a charge-to-mass ratio of 1.758820 × 10^11 C/kg.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Discovery of Protons and Neutrons
text:
Discovery of Protons and Neutrons

Protons were discovered by Ernest Rutherford in 1919, and neutrons were discovered by James Chadwick in 1932. Protons have a positive charge, while neutrons have no charge.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Discovery of Protons and Neutrons in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Thomson Model of Atom
text:
Thomson Model of Atom

Key terms: Thomson model, positively charged sphere, electron distribution

J.J. Thomson proposed the first atomic model in 1898, where electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere. However, it couldn't explain the stability of atoms.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Thomson Model of Atom in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Rutherford Model of Atom
text:
Rutherford Model of Atom

Key terms: Rutherford model, nucleus, electrons, protons, neutrons

Ernest Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom in 1911, where electrons orbit around a dense, positively charged nucleus containing protons and neutrons.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rutherford Model of Atom in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Atomic Number and Mass Number
text:
Atomic Number and Mass Number

Key terms: atomic number, mass number, atomic mass

The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus, while the mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons. The atomic mass is approximately equal to the mass number.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Atomic Number and Mass Number in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Isotopes
text:
Isotopes

Key terms: isotopes, atomic number, atomic mass, neutrons

Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different mass numbers due to varying numbers of neutrons. They have the same atomic number but different atomic masses.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Isotopes in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Ionization Energy
text:
Ionization Energy

Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated atom or molecule. It depends on the number of electrons and their arrangement in the atom.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ionization Energy in Grade 11 Chemistry.

text:

Key terms: alpha particle, nucleus, gold foil

Rutherford discovered the nucleus of an atom by bombarding a thin gold foil with alpha particles. Most passed through undeflected, some were deflected slightly, and a few bounced back, indicating a small, positively charged core at the atom's center.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom
text:
Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom

Key terms: nucleus, electron, atomic model

Rutherford proposed that an atom consists of a dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by electrons moving in circular orbits. This model explained the results of his gold foil experiment.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Atomic Number and Mass Number

Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus, determining its chemical properties. Mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons, representing the isotope's mass.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Atomic Number and Mass Number in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Isobars and Isotopes

Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers, while isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to varying neutron counts.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Isobars and Isotopes in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Drawbacks of Rutherford's Model

Dual Nature of Electromagnetic Radiation

Electromagnetic radiation exhibits both wave-like and particle-like properties, with wave properties including frequency, wavelength, and speed.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dual Nature of Electromagnetic Radiation in Grade 11 Chemistry.

text:
Atomic Spectra and Bohr's Model

Bohr improved upon Rutherford's model by incorporating the dual nature of electromagnetic radiation and experimental results from atomic spectra, leading to the development of his atomic model.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Atomic Spectra and Bohr's Model in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Frequency and Wavelength of Electromagnetic Radiation

Key terms: frequency, wavelength, speed of light

Frequency (ν) is the number of waves passing a point per second (Hz), while wavelength (λ) is the distance between successive waves. They are inversely proportional, and the speed of light (c) relates them as c = νλ.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Frequency and Wavelength of Electromagnetic Radiation
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Frequency and Wavelength of Electromagnetic Radiation in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Wavenumber and its Units

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Wavenumber and its Units in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Photoelectric Effect

Electrons are emitted from a metal surface when light of sufficient frequency strikes it. The kinetic energy of emitted electrons depends on the light's frequency, not its intensity.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Photoelectric Effect in Grade 11 Chemistry.

text:
Planck's Quantum Theory

Key terms: quantum, Planck's constant, frequency

Max Planck proposed that energy is quantized, meaning it can only be absorbed or emitted in discrete packets called quanta. The energy of a quantum is proportional to its frequency (E = hν).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Planck's Quantum Theory in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Dual Nature of Electromagnetic Radiation

Electromagnetic radiation exhibits both wave-like and particle-like properties, depending on the experiment. It behaves as waves when propagating and as particles (photons) when interacting with matter.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Dual Nature of Electromagnetic Radiation in Grade 11 Chemistry.

text:

Photon energy can be calculated using the equation E = hf, where h is Planck's constant and f is the frequency of the photon. In the given problem, the energy of a 300 nm photon is calculated as 4.969 × 10^-19 J.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Photon Energy Calculation in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Minimum Energy to Remove Electron
text:

Key terms: minimum energy, electron, kinetic energy, photon energy

The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from sodium is calculated by subtracting the kinetic energy of the emitted electrons from the energy of one mole of photons. In this case, it is 2.31 × 10^5 J mol^-1.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Minimum Energy to Remove Electron in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Maximum Wavelength for Photoelectron Emission
text:
Maximum Wavelength for Photoelectron Emission

Key terms: maximum wavelength, photoelectron, Planck's constant, speed of light

The maximum wavelength that will cause a photoelectron to be emitted can be calculated using the equation E = hc/λ, where E is the minimum energy needed to remove an electron, h is Planck's constant, c is the speed of light, and λ is the wavelength. In this problem, the maximum wavelength is calculated to be 517 nm, which corresponds to green light.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Maximum Wavelength for Photoelectron Emission in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Kinetic Energy of Emitted Electron
text:
Kinetic Energy of Emitted Electron

Key terms: kinetic energy, emitted electron, Planck's constant, frequency, threshold frequency

The kinetic energy of an emitted electron can be calculated using Einstein's equation KE = h(ν - ν0), where h is Planck's constant, ν is the frequency of the incident radiation, and ν0 is the threshold frequency for the metal. In this problem, the kinetic energy of the emitted electron is calculated to be 1.988 × 10^-19 J.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Kinetic Energy of Emitted Electron in Grade 11 Chemistry.

Electronic Energy Levels: Atomic Spectra

Atomic spectra are produced when atoms or molecules emit or absorb radiation in various regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. The study of emission or absorption spectra is referred to as spectroscopy.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electronic Energy Levels: Atomic Spectra in Grade 11 Chemistry.

text:
Line Spectrum of Hydrogen

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Bohr's Model for Hydrogen Atom
text:
Bohr's Model for Hydrogen Atom

Key terms: Bohr's model, hydrogen atom, stationary states, angular momentum

Bohr's model for the hydrogen atom is based on the following postulates: the electron can move around the nucleus in a circular path of fixed radius and energy, the energy of an electron in the orbit does not change with time, the frequency of radiation absorbed or emitted when transition occurs between two stationary states is given by Bohr's frequency rule, and the angular momentum of an electron is quantised.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Bohr's Theory for Hydrogen Atom
text:
Bohr's Theory for Hydrogen Atom

Key terms: Bohr's model, electron orbits, line spectra

Bohr's theory explains the stability and line spectra of hydrogen atom using fixed electron orbits. It assumes electrons move in circular paths around the nucleus, absorbing or emitting energy in discrete amounts.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Energy and Radius of Hydrogen-like Species
text:
Energy and Radius of Hydrogen-like Species

Limitations of Bohr's Model

Bohr's model fails to explain the finer details of hydrogen spectra, spectra of other atoms, chemical bonding, and the splitting of spectral lines in the presence of magnetic or electric fields.

text:
Dual Behaviour of Matter

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle
text:
Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle

Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that it is impossible to simultaneously determine the exact position and momentum of an electron. This principle is significant only for microscopic objects.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle in Grade 11 Chemistry.

text:
Failure of Bohr's Model

Bohr's model fails because it ignores the wave character of electrons and contradicts Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. It is not suitable for extending to other atoms.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Failure of Bohr's Model in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
text:
Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle

Key terms: uncertainty, position, velocity, electron

It's impossible to simultaneously measure the exact position and velocity of an electron in an atom. The more precisely one property is measured, the less precisely the other can be known.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
text:
Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom

Key terms: quantum mechanics, Schrödinger's equation, wave-particle duality, uncertainty principle

This model, based on Schrödinger's equation, describes the behavior of electrons in atoms, accounting for wave-particle duality and the uncertainty principle.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Quantum Numbers
text:
Quantum Numbers

Key terms: quantum numbers, atomic orbitals, electronic structure

Quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms) describe the energy, shape, orientation, and spin of atomic orbitals, respectively. They help explain the electronic structure of atoms.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Quantum Numbers in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Atomic Orbitals
text:
Atomic Orbitals

Key terms: atomic orbitals, probability, quantum numbers

Atomic orbitals are mathematical functions that describe the probability of finding an electron in a specific region around the nucleus. They are characterized by quantum numbers.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Atomic Orbitals in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Electron Spin
text:
Electron Spin

Key terms: electron spin, up, down

Electrons have an intrinsic spin, which can be either 'up' or 'down'. Two electrons in the same orbital must have opposite spins.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electron Spin in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Energy Levels in Atoms
text:
Energy Levels in Atoms

Key terms: energy levels, quantized, Schrödinger equation

Electrons in atoms can only have specific, quantized energy levels. These energy levels are determined by the quantum numbers and the Schrödinger equation.

metadata.subject: Chemistry

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Wave-Particle Duality
text:
Wave-Particle Duality

Key terms: wave-particle duality, electrons, quantum mechanics

Electrons exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties. This duality is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Electron Probability Density
text:
Electron Probability Density

Key terms: wave function, probability density, orbital

The square of the wave function (|ψ|^2) gives the probability density of finding an electron at a point in an atom. It varies with the distance from the nucleus and has different shapes for different orbitals.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electron Probability Density in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Nodal Surfaces
text:
Nodal Surfaces

Key terms: probability density, nodes, principal quantum number

Regions where the probability density function reduces to zero are called nodal surfaces or nodes. The number of nodes increases with the principal quantum number (n).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Nodal Surfaces in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Orbital Shapes
text:
Orbital Shapes

Key terms: orbital, s-orbital, p-orbital, d-orbital

Orbitals have different shapes depending on their quantum numbers. s-orbitals are spherical, p-orbitals have two lobes, and d-orbitals have complex shapes with multiple lobes.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Orbital Shapes in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Orbital Energies
text:
Orbital Energies

Key terms: orbital energy, principal quantum number, azimuthal quantum number

In a hydrogen atom, orbital energy increases with the principal quantum number (n). In multi-electron atoms, energy also depends on the azimuthal quantum number (l), with s-orbitals having lower energy than p-orbitals, which have lower energy than d-orbitals.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Orbital Energies in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Effective Nuclear Charge
text:
Effective Nuclear Charge

Key terms: effective nuclear charge, Zeff, azimuthal quantum number

The net positive charge experienced by an outer electron due to the attraction of the nucleus and the repulsion of inner shell electrons is called the effective nuclear charge (Zeff). It decreases with increasing azimuthal quantum number (l).

metadata.subject: Chemistry

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Orbital Energy based on (n + l)
text:
Orbital Energy based on (n + l)

The energy of an orbital depends on (n + l), with lower values having lower energy. If two orbitals have the same (n + l), the one with lower n has lower energy.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Orbital Energy based on (n + l) in Grade 11 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Aufbau Principle

Electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy, starting with the lowest energy orbital available.

No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers, meaning no more than two electrons can occupy the same orbital with opposite spins.

Electrons fill orbitals with the same energy (subshell) one by one before pairing up, to achieve the highest possible spin multiplicity.

Resonance occurs when a molecule can be represented by two or more Lewis structures. The actual molecule has a hybrid structure with energy lower than any single Lewis structure, and it averages the properties of all resonance structures.

Forces between atoms lead to bond formation. Attractive forces (like NA-eB) bring atoms closer, while repulsive forces (like eA-eB) push them apart. In a bond, attractive forces are stronger than repulsive forces.

In ethyne, both carbon atoms undergo sp-hybridisation. One sp hybrid orbital of each carbon overlaps axially to form a sigma bond, while the other sp hybrid orbital overlaps with the half-filled s orbital of hydrogen atoms. The two unhybridised p orbitals of each carbon overlap sidewise to form two pi bonds.

text:

Key terms: Calorimetry, Constant Pressure, Enthalpy Change

A technique used to measure heat change at constant pressure. The heat absorbed or evolved at constant pressure is equal to the enthalpy change (∆H). An open calorimeter is used, where the reaction is carried out under atmospheric pressure.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Calorimeter for Heat Measurement
text:
Calorimeter for Heat Measurement

Key terms: calorimeter, heat of reaction, enthalpy of reaction, exothermic, endothermic

A calorimeter is used to measure heat change at constant pressure. The heat absorbed or evolved, qp, at constant pressure is also called the heat of reaction or enthalpy of reaction, ∆rH. In an exothermic reaction, heat is evolved and the system loses heat to the surroundings, making qp negative and ∆rH negative. Conversely, in an endothermic reaction, heat is absorbed, making qp positive and ∆rH positive.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Enthalpy Change of a Reaction
text:
Enthalpy Change of a Reaction

Key terms: enthalpy change, reaction enthalpy, enthalpy of products, enthalpy of reactants

The enthalpy change accompanying a reaction is called the reaction enthalpy, ∆rH. It is given by the difference between the sum of enthalpies of products and the sum of enthalpies of reactants, with each term multiplied by its stoichiometric coefficient.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Chemistry | Standard Enthalpy of Reaction
text:
Standard Enthalpy of Reaction

Key terms: standard enthalpy of reaction, standard state, ∆H

The standard enthalpy of reaction is the enthalpy change for a reaction when all the participating substances are in their standard states. It is denoted by ∆H and is used to plan heating or cooling requirements for industrial chemical reactions and to calculate temperature dependence of equilibrium constants.

Enthalpy Changes during Phase Transformations

Key terms: phase transformations, enthalpy of fusion, enthalpy of vaporization, ∆fusH, ∆vapH

Phase transformations involve energy changes. For example, melting ice requires heat, and the enthalpy change for this process is called the enthalpy of fusion, ∆fusH. Similarly, evaporation of water requires heat, and the enthalpy change for this process is called the enthalpy of vaporization, ∆vapH.

Liquids in a closed container reach an equilibrium where the rate of evaporation equals the rate of condensation, resulting in a constant vapour pressure. The boiling point is the temperature at which this occurs at atmospheric pressure.
